Dear Senator Hickman, Representative Supica and esteemed Members
of the Veterans and Legal Affairs Committee, I am Representative Barbara Bagshaw from Windham, District I06 and am here today to
present testimony in support of LD 349 An Act to Repeal the Laws
that Allow Same-day Voter Registration.

I have personally witnessed firsthand the challenges posed by same-day voter registration. During recent elections, I have observed voter lines extending for over an hour, particularly during the last presidential
election, when the lines wove around the back of the building. Many
people, unable to wait due to work or other obligations, gave up and left without casting their votes. This speaks to the strain on both voters and election workers, which is only exacerbated by the administrative
burden of same-day registration.

Poll staffing is already difficult, and adding the responsibility of sameday voter registration further compounds the challenges for election
officials, poll workers, and volunteers. This is why I believe ending
same-day voter registration is critical for ensuring efficient, accurate, and fair elections in Maine.
Same-day registration can lead to confusion and disorganization on
Election Day and administrative chaos. As Sandwich, Massachusetts,
town clerk Taylor White explained in 2017, deadlines exist to help election officials prepare accurate voter lists and conduct orderly
elections. When voters show up to register and vote on the same day, it
introduces logistical complications that can undermine this process. Without sufficient time to verify eligibility, maintain updated records, and address potential issues, election integrity and efficiency can be compromised.
Doug Ellis, an election administrator from Broadwater County,
Montana, testified during a 2021 hearing that same-day registration
places a significant burden on election officials. He described elections
as one of the most challenging parts of his job, largely due to the difficulties of processing registrations and ensuring accurate vote counts simultaneously. The need to input voter information while managing high turnout can create delays, errors, and frustration for both officials and voters.
In Maine, we face similar challenges. Smaller communities and rural
areas, in particular, often lack the resources and staffing necessary to handle the influx of same-day registrants, leading to delays, inaccuracies, and logistical strain.
Another concern is that same-day registration may encourage illinformed voting. As Kevin Deitrich highlighted in a 2022 article for Nevada Policy, individuals who haven't registered ahead of time may be
less informed about the issues on the ballot. Similarly, Matthew Gagnon,
writing in the Bangor Daily News in 201 1, noted that registering ahead
of time is a sign that voters have put thought into their participation.

Gagnon argued that those who register at the last minute may be less
engaged, which could result in impulsive or uninformed voting.
Additionally, when voters rush through the registration and voting
process on the same day, it increases the likelihood of errors, provisional
ballots, or challenges to their eligibility, creating further complications for election officials.
I recently had favorable communication with four town clerks from
municipalities in Maine who support eliminating Election Day voter
registration at the polls. They felt that, administratively, it would be a lot
easier on them to manage and we discussed a potential compromise. The
compromise would be ending voter registration on the Thursday before Election Day, which would also coincide with the close of early in-
person voting.
With a few extra days, we could address many of the concerns
surrounding same-day registration. Currently, 21 states allow some sort
of lead time cut-off to Election Day. All of the other states have deadlines from 10 days up to 45 days prior, with the most popular being
30 days prior. They agreed that having it coincide with the last day to
absentee vote, which is the Thursday before Election Day would
simplify the process. Potentially, they would not have to hire and train as
many registrars to work at the polls, and it would cut down on having an
extra line in the hallway and reduce the number of duplicate
registrations.
Again, this would alleviate the staffing strain by giving officials time to
verify registrations and maintain accurate voter lists. Improve the flow
of voters on Election Day, reduce wait times and ensure more people can successfully cast their ballots; ensuring a more efficient and accurate process, with fewer errors and challenges and reduce financial and resource burdens on election offices for smaller communities.
Another consideration is the inability to adequately verify eligibility
which may undermine the accuracy of the voter rolls, potentially
damaging public trust in the electoral process.

For the sake of Maine voters and our dedicated town clerks, I urge this
committee to support LD 349 and repeal same-day voter registration. \
Our goal should be an electoral process that is efficient, accurate, and free from administrative chaos. Ending same-day registration will help
achieve that goal, ensuring smoother operations on Election Day and
better outcomes for all involved.
Thank you for your time, and I would be happy to answer any questions
aw" Yours truly,

In Maine, this translates to about 33,000 people age 70 and older who do not hold a current driver's license. And this estimate was made before COVID!
Older people who don't drive or have access to public transportation have to rely on others to get to medical appointments, church, the grocery store, the bank, and to the hairdresser. TESTIMONY OF MICHAEL KEBEDE, ESQ. LD 349 - Ought Not to Pass
An Act to Repeal the Laws That Allow Same-day Voter Registration
JOINT STANDING COMMITTEE ON VETERANS AND LEGAL AFFAIRS
February 10, 2025
Senator Hickman, Representative Supica and distinguished members of the Joint Standing Committee on Veterans and Legal Affairs, greetings. My name is Michael Kebede, and I am Policy Director at the American Civil Liberties Union of Maine, a statewide organization committed to advancing and preserving civil liberties guaranteed by the Maine and U.S. Constitutions. On behalf of our members, I urge you to reject LD 349.
The ACLU of Maine is committed to protecting and expanding voting rights. Our democracy is stronger when as many people as possible have a voice. That is why we consistently urge you to consider ways to strengthen and expand, rather than constrict, participation in the voting process.
Same day voter registration is good public policy and there is no reason to repeal it. Maine law has permitted same day voter registration since 1973, when it passed with bipartisan support in a Republican-controlled legislature. It has worked well for over fifty years, particularly for people who have moved recently, are busy, have multiple jobs, and benefit from the convenience of registration and voting in a streamlined fashion.1
1 History of "Same-Day' Voter Registration in Maine, Bangor Daily News ( Nov. 5, 2011), https://www.bangordailynews.com/2011/11/05/news/history-of-same-

Page 2 of 2
Not only has the legislature rejected similar legislation, but so have the voters. In a 2011 "people's veto," which passed with 60% of the statewide vote and garnered majorities in every county, Mainers roundly rejected an effort to eliminate same day voter registration.2
LD 349 also significantly relaxes the rules around challenging voter registration and wardens' ability to keep polling places running smoothly. This proposal would disrupt elections in Maine in three ways. First, it repeals the provision that requires those who want to monitor voter registration at the polling place tell the clerk ahead of time in writing. In practice this usually means that a person inform the clerk the day before, which seems very reasonable. Second, this proposal repeals the instruction that says a person who is monitoring voter registration in the polling place cannot handle voter registration cards, handle the registrar's files, or handle the clerk's files. Allowing election monitors to handle other voters' registration cards or the clerk's files would dramatically decrease the security of the Election Day process. And third, the proposal repeals the law that says a warden may request fewer polling place registration monitors if the work of the registrar or clerk appears to be inhibited.
Maine has effective election laws that promote secure elections characterized by integrity and high voter turnout. I urge this committee to protect and expand Maine's election laws, rather than repeal voting laws that work well.
Please reject this harmful bill.

Sen. Hickman, Rep. Supica, and members of the Veterans and Legal Affairs Committee, thank you for the opportunity to submit testimony before you today. I'm Penny Morrell, taxpayer and citizen of the Town of Belgrade, Maine.
I support L.D. 349, "An Act to Repeal the Laws That Allow Same-day Voter Registration".
I have worked the polls in Belgrade. Same-day voter registration adds a state of unnecessary chaos for both the election staff and voters. Those wishing to register to vote on election day need to go to a special place having additional staff to facilitate the transaction. It sometimes leads to long lines because of the time involved making sure the voter isn't already registered, filling out the necessary paperwork, perhaps enrolling in a political party, and then getting in line to receive ballots to vote. All this, done before election day, will be advantageous to all involved.
It also alleviates one way for voters to cheat. In the past, I believe same-day registration has allowed cheaters to register in several municipalities with no way for election wardens and staff to know. It just makes sense to protect the integrity of the vote by repealing election-day voting.
I urge this committee to vote "ought to pass" on LD 349. Thank you.
